# iOS Performance & Battery Optimization

> Derived from the Auditor's [ViLM — iOS Performance & Battery Audit (Engineering Review)](https://app.notion.com/p/3afadccaf42881a5b9fbf5e3c26af9c6), authored by Antigravity in the QA/Auditor role. **Every finding was independently re-verified against the source on 2026-08-01 before being written here** — three required correction. Status: In Review, awaiting Human Operator approval. No code until Status = Approved.
## Intention
Reduce CPU, GPU, disk I/O and memory pressure in ViLM on iOS so that sustained operations (contact-sheet grids, duplicate scans, library transfers) stop pinning performance cores, overheating the device and draining battery — **without altering any functional contract**.
Per personal standards: characterization tests precede refactoring, no behaviour changes inside a refactor commit, and layout is validated on a physical iPhone before merge.
## Verification of the audit
The audit is sound in mechanism. Its *scope* was understated in two places and one energy claim is inaccurate.
| # | Audit claim | Verified? | Correction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | 16 concurrent `AVAssetImageGenerator`, `AppComponents.swift` 65–180 | ✅ **Confirmed** | Generator at `:175`, `maximumSize` 800×600 at `:177`, `image(at:)` at `:180` |
| F2 | 3 sites at `.userInitiated` | ⚠️ **Confirmed, badly undercounted** | **20 sites across 12 files.** Only **2** uses of `.utility`/`.background` exist in the entire app |
| F3 | Per-item `save()` in fingerprint loop | ✅ **Confirmed** | `DuplicateDetectionView.swift:362` |
| F4 | 192 MB + 96 MB NSCache = ~288 MB | ⚠️ **Confirmed, incomplete** | `ProfileImageView.swift:27` (192 MB), `AppComponents.swift:199` (96 MB), **plus a third cache the audit missed** — `DashboardComponents.swift:181` sets `countLimit = 500` with **no cost limit at all** |
| F5 | Redundant I/O "on main thread state changes" | ❌ **Energy claim inaccurate** | `AssetGridView.swift:644` already runs inside `Task.detached(priority: .utility)` — off-main **and** already downgraded. The real defect is that file size is never persisted, so every sort re-stats every file |
| F6 | Cache dimensions in the `assets` table | ⚠️ **Mechanism confirmed, remedy understated** | 12 `AVURLAsset(` sites. But **the columns do not exist** — see below |
### ⚠️ The assets table has no metadata columns
F5 and F6 both recommend persisting size, duration and dimensions "into SQLite (assets table)". Verified against `LibraryStore.swift:114-218` and `Asset.swift`, the `assets` table contains only:
```javascript
id, relative_path, file_name, status, created_at, tags, external_link,
notes, rating, video_name, episode, season_number, episode_number,
play_count, last_played_at
```
**There is no ****`file_size`****, ****`duration`****, ****`width`****, ****`height`****, ****`codec`**** or ****`modified_at`****.** So F5 and F6 are **schema additions plus scanner work plus a backfill migration for existing libraries** — substantially more than "cache it in the table", and they should be sized accordingly.
> **Cross-system conflict (Article I).** The ViLM application charter's data-model section claims the assets table holds `file_size, duration, width, height, codec, modified_at`. It does not. Raised, not silently corrected — tracked as **C1**.
## ⚠️ P0 prerequisite — establish a baseline first
**No performance baseline exists.** Every acceptance criterion below is expressed as a relative improvement, and none can be evaluated without a before-measurement. The audit's own action plan calls for Instruments validation but does not require a baseline capture.
**No optimisation task may be marked Done before its baseline is recorded.** Capture on a physical iPhone via Instruments (Energy Log + CPU Profiler + Allocations), against a fixed reference library, recording:
- Energy impact and CPU% during a 4×4 contact-sheet grid render
- Energy, wall-clock and peak memory for a duplicate scan over a fixed video count
- Peak resident memory during sustained actor-grid scrolling
- Thermal state transitions during a sustained duplicate scan
The reference library, device model and iOS version are recorded with the numbers; comparisons are only valid against the same trio.
## F1 · Unthrottled 16-frame concurrent video decoding
**Location:** `AppComponents.swift:175-180` (`DetailGridView` / `FrameExtractView`).
**Mechanism.** A 4×4 grid renders 16 cells, each constructing its own `AVAssetImageGenerator` (`maximumSize` 800×600) and awaiting `generator.image(at:)`. Sixteen independent hardware decode paths start at once, and results are uncached, so any re-render decodes everything again.
**Direction.** Batch via `generateCGImagesAsynchronously`, bound concurrency behind a `TaskGroup` or actor-serialised queue, and cache decoded images.
**Acceptance criteria**
- Concurrent generator count is explicitly bounded and the bound is a named constant, not incidental.
- Re-rendering an already-viewed grid performs **zero** additional decodes (cache hit).
- Energy impact and CPU% during grid render measurably below baseline on device.
- The rendered grid is visually identical — same frames, same timestamps, same order.
- Scrolling away mid-decode cancels outstanding work rather than orphaning it.
## F2 · Batch work runs at `.userInitiated` QoS
**Scope corrected: 20 sites across 12 files** — `ActorGridView`, `ActorLibraryExportView`, `ActorLibraryImportView` (×2), `ActorSyncView` (×2), `AppComponents`, `ContentView`, `DashboardComponents`, `DashboardView`, `DuplicateDetectionView` (×2), `LibraryBackupView` (×4), `LibraryStatsView`, `LibraryTransferView` (×3).
**Mechanism.** `.userInitiated` signals "the user is blocked on this", so the scheduler pins performance cores at high clock. Correct for a tap-to-response action; wrong for a multi-minute fingerprint scan across 1,000+ videos. With only 2 non-`.userInitiated` sites app-wide, this is a **codebase-wide default**, not three oversights.
**Direction.** Classify each of the 20 sites as *interactive* (user is waiting, keep `.userInitiated`) or *batch* (long-running, downgrade to `.utility`; `.background` where the user is not watching at all). Establish a documented convention so new work inherits it.
**Acceptance criteria**
- All 20 sites are classified, with the rationale recorded per site.
- Long-running scans run at `.utility` or lower; no batch operation remains at `.userInitiated`.
- Progress UI stays responsive — a downgraded scan must not make the progress indicator stutter.
- Measured reduction in thermal-state escalation during a sustained duplicate scan.
- A convention is documented in the repo so the default does not regress.
## F3 · Per-item serialisation in the fingerprint loop
**Location:** `DuplicateDetectionView.swift:362` — `caches[owner]!.save()` inside the per-video loop.
**Mechanism.** A full JSON encode and disk write per processed video; a 500-video scan performs 500+ write cycles to flash.
**Direction.** Flush every 25–50 items, and on completion **and** cancellation.
**Acceptance criteria**
- Write count during an N-video scan is bounded by roughly `N/25`, verified by counting writes in a test.
- **No cache loss on cancellation or error** — a partially completed scan retains work up to the last flush.
- Measured reduction in disk-write volume for a fixed scan.
## F4 · Uncapped and oversized bitmap caches
**Locations:** `ProfileImageView.swift:27` (192 MB), `AppComponents.swift:199` (96 MB), `DashboardComponents.swift:181` (`countLimit = 500`, **no cost limit**).
**Mechanism.** ~288 MB of fixed cost limits, plus a third cache bounded only by object count. On a 3 GB device this invites Jetsam termination, page compression and background-app eviction. A count-bounded bitmap cache is effectively unbounded in bytes, since cost varies with image size.
**Direction.** Scale limits from `ProcessInfo.processInfo.physicalMemory`, give the third cache a cost limit, and respond to memory-pressure notifications by evicting.
**Acceptance criteria**
- No cache uses a hardcoded absolute byte limit; all derive from device RAM.
- Every bitmap cache has a `totalCostLimit`, and cost is the decoded byte size rather than object count.
- Caches evict on `didReceiveMemoryWarning` / memory-pressure source.
- Peak resident memory during sustained scrolling stays under a stated ceiling on the lowest supported device.
- No functional regression: images still appear, and cache-miss paths still fetch correctly.
## F5 · File attributes re-read on every size sort
**Location:** `AssetGridView.swift:644`; also `DuplicateDetectionView.swift:269`, `AppComponents.swift:207`, and 5 sites in `LibraryCore`.
**Correction to the audit.** The claim of "main thread state changes" is wrong — this path already runs in `Task.detached(priority: .utility)`. The genuine defect is that file size is **not persisted**, so sorting by size re-stats every file in the library on each trigger change.
**Direction.** Persist `file_size` and `modified_at` during scan; let GRDB do `ORDER BY` against an index.
**Acceptance criteria**
- `assets` gains `file_size` and `modified_at`, populated during scan.
- Sorting by size issues **no** `attributesOfItem` calls — asserted in a test.
- A backfill migration populates existing libraries without a full rescan, and is resumable.
- Sort order is byte-identical to today's for an unchanged library (characterization test).
- Stale entries (file changed on disk) are detected and refreshed.
## F6 · Repeated AVFoundation header parsing
**Locations:** 12 `AVURLAsset(` sites — `InspectorView.swift:1010,1026`, `DuplicateDetectionView.swift:273`, `AppComponents.swift:76`, `EditVideoView.swift:256`, plus `ContactSheetService`, `VideoEditingService`, `VideoTransferService`.
**Mechanism.** Duration, track list, natural size and preferred transform are re-loaded by reopening the file and re-parsing container atoms on hover and selection.
**Direction.** Persist duration, dimensions and codec during scan; read from SQLite for display.
**Acceptance criteria**
- `assets` gains `duration`, `width`, `height`, `codec`, populated during scan.
- Inspector display of duration and dimensions performs **no** `AVURLAsset` construction.
- Editing and transcoding paths still construct assets as needed — only *display* reads are served from the database.
- Backfill migration as per F5, sharing the same mechanism.
- Values match what AVFoundation reports today (characterization test over a fixture set).
## Test strategy (Article III + personal standards)
- **Characterization first.** Before touching any of this, capture current behaviour — frame timestamps for F1, sort order for F5, reported metadata for F6. These tests must pass unchanged afterwards.
- **No behaviour change inside a refactor commit.** Optimisation and functional change never share a commit.
- **Failure states, not happy paths.** Cancellation mid-scan (F3), memory pressure (F4), missing or corrupt files (F5/F6), and cache eviction under load must all be exercised.
- **Executed, not assumed.** The Auditor runs the suite via CLI (`swift test --package-path ViLM/LibraryCore`) and reads real output.
- **Device validation.** Instruments on a physical iPhone before merge, per personal standards. Simulator numbers are not evidence for energy claims.
## Delivery phases
1. **Phase 0 · Baseline.** Instruments capture + characterization tests. Blocks everything else.
2. **Phase 1 · Highest energy yield.** F1 (decode throttling + cache) and F2 (QoS classification). The audit recommends these first and the verification supports it — F2 in particular is 20 sites, so it is broad but mechanical.
3. **Phase 2 · I/O and memory.** F3 (batched flush) and F4 (adaptive cache limits). Self-contained, low risk.
4. **Phase 3 · Schema-backed metadata.** F5 and F6 together — they share one migration, one scanner change and one backfill. Largest and riskiest; sequenced last deliberately.
## Decisions — Human Operator
### ✅ D1 — Reference baseline
**iPhone 16 Pro**, against a reference library of:
- **~1,300 videos**, ~450 MB each — approximately **585 GB** total
- **~1,300 actor profiles**, ~2 JPGs each — approximately **2,600 images**
All comparisons are valid only against this device, this library shape, and a recorded iOS version. Any number quoted without that trio is not evidence.
> **Implication for F5/F6.** A backfill touches ~1,300 files. Stat-ing them is trivial; opening each to parse container atoms is not. This shapes the delivery recommendation below.
### ✅ D2 — Improvement target
**"Measurably better" is the acceptance bar; 20% is the aim.** A change that measurably improves energy or memory is accepted even below 20% — the target guides effort, it does not gate merge.
- Where a finding lands short of 20%, the residual opportunity is **recorded in the backlog** rather than dropped.
- Note that the right metric differs per finding: F2's gain shows up in **thermal state and energy**, not wall-clock — a correctly downgraded batch scan may take *longer* while consuming less. Do not read that as a regression.
### ✅ D3 — Eager backfill
**Eager**, accepting a slower first launch after upgrade in exchange for a consistently snappy app thereafter.
Required because eager backfill over ~1,300 files is user-visible:
- A **progress indicator** stating what is happening and how far along it is.
- **Resumable** — killing the app mid-backfill must not restart from zero, and must not leave half-populated rows indistinguishable from un-backfilled ones.
- **Cancellable**, degrading to lazy population for whatever remains.
- The app stays **usable during backfill** — features that do not need the new columns must not block on it.
### ✅ D4 — Phase 3 delivery: one migration, two population stages *(Engineer's recommendation, accepted)*
**Ship all six columns in a single migration, but populate them in two independently resumable stages.**
**Why one migration.** Two migrations means two schema versions, two upgrade paths and — under D3's eager policy — **two slow first launches**. Adding columns is cheap; adding them twice is not.
**Why two population stages.** The two groups have sharply different cost and risk profiles:
| Stage | Columns | Source | Cost over 1,300 files | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A · fast** | `file_size`, `modified_at` | `FileManager` attributes | milliseconds | very low |
| **B · slow** | `duration`, `width`, `height`, `codec` | `AVURLAsset` header parse | 1,300 file opens + atom parsing | codec-dependent; can fail on damaged or exotic files |
Stage A delivers F5's win almost immediately. Stage B runs after, with its own progress and resumability. **If Stage B proves slow or unreliable on some codecs, it can be deferred or made lazy without a second migration** — the columns already exist and simply stay null.
This also gives a natural task split for the backlog without splitting the schema.
## Corrections raised
- **C1 · Charter data model is inaccurate.** ✅ **Corrected in Notion 2026-08-01.** The ViLM application charter claimed the assets table holds `file_size, duration, width, height, codec, modified_at`. Verified absent from `LibraryStore.swift:114-218`; the charter now lists the columns that actually exist and notes that this specification's Phase 3 will add the metadata columns.
